A1.justification: Both PDFs describe MERIT and CORAL. Their main text, equations, figures, tables, and Appendices A–F are readable and support reliable comparison, including matching material relocated around the references.

before.justification: Sections 3–4 and Appendix E report original retrieval experiments, ablations, out-of-distribution evaluations, and error analyses.

after.justification: V2 retains those empirical results and adds human-preference results and retrieval performance grouped by condition count.

M1.justification: CORAL retains the same contrastive learning, visual reconstruction, language reconstruction, and overall training objective. Section 4.1 clarifies masking notation without changing the procedure.

E1.justification: MERIT and the external retrieval benchmarks remain unchanged. The new studies reuse MERIT; queries containing two, three, and four conditions were already represented in v1.

E2.justification: Table 11 introduces a direct human-preference comparison between CORAL, GME-Qwen2VL-2B, LamRA-Qwen2.5VL-7B, and BGE-VL-7B. These comparator families already appeared elsewhere, and the original comparison tables retain their membership.

E3.justification: Appendix E.6 adds a protocol using 100 randomly sampled MERIT items, five annotators, Choice@1/Choice@3, and similarity-score credit for duplicate selections. E.7 adds evaluation grouped by condition count. Previously documented splits and training settings remain unchanged.

E4.justification: New Appendices E.6–E.7 examine human preference and sensitivity to the number of query conditions. Existing modality/input ablations, distribution-shift tests, language analyses, and error cases are retained.

E5.justification: V2 adds average human-selection rates as an evaluation metric, but introduces no repeated-run or seed reporting, confidence intervals, error bars, or significance tests.

E6.justification: Tables 11–12 add results: CORAL receives 53.6% Choice@1 and 58.9% Choice@3, while GME achieves the highest reported four-condition R@5 of 36.84 among the models in Table 12. Existing benchmark and ablation values remain unchanged.

T1.justification: Equations (1)–(5) retain the same mathematical content. The masking-function notation and distinction between E and e are clarified; no substantive definition, derivation, theorem, or proof is added.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and conclusion retain the same dataset novelty, diagnosis of neglected conditional information, and CORAL contributions, including the 45.9% improvement claim and validation across eight retrieval tasks.

C2.justification: Appendix E.7 newly interprets weak four-condition retrieval as evidence of combinatorial difficulty. Its general decreasing-performance interpretation has exceptions between two and three conditions in Table 12. Existing mechanism explanations and Appendix F limitations remain unchanged.

D1.justification: Data-generation prompts, annotation instructions, implementation settings, hardware, hyperparameters, and reported code/data access information are retained. Removing 310,000 from Table 9's caption does not remove the training-size disclosure elsewhere.

R1.justification: All 105 earlier references are retained and four works are added, including Decoder-only LLMs Can Be Masked Auto-encoders, Mixed-R1, mm-expert, and a GPT-4o image-generation study. Citation additions do not substantially revise the related-work narrative or novelty positioning.

P1.justification: References move before the appendices, two appendix subsections are added, and masking notation, a caption typo, and author/conference information receive limited edits. Most prose and section organization remain intact.

P2.justification: Figure 2 is revised, including rearranged query examples and labels. Tables 11–12 are added, the title block changes, and existing appendix figures and tables are repaginated. The remaining visual presentation is largely preserved.

improvement.justification: The new human-preference and condition-count studies address evidence absent from v1, but their net benefit is uncertain. Table 11 assigns duplicate-hit credit using cross-model similarity scores without discussing calibration. Table 12's GME R@5 breakdown of 53.12/55.91/36.84 is not reconciled with the retained 47.13 aggregate in Table 2, and subgroup sizes or different settings are unspecified. These reporting ambiguities limit confidence in the added evidence, while the core paper remains largely unchanged.
